input: I am about to write the Stripe launch-criterion recommendation for the P1 review. Launch criterion two says Stripe handles paid-tier billing before launch; production has Stripe deliberately not configured; the billing mechanism itself is built and metering on every loop, which I verified today from live calls. The completion plan treats activation as triggered by the first paying consumer. The review recommends amending the criterion, and my recommendation agrees: amend criterion two to read that the billing mechanism is proven and activation is a runbook triggered by the first paying consumer, with the activation runbook written and the Stripe account prerequisites, which depend on the company incorporation, tracked as founder wall-clock items. The alternative, activating Stripe pre-launch against zero customers, adds configuration surface and compliance weight with no revenue to meter. I see no strong argument for the alternative but I am writing a recommendation that resolves a founder-named launch criterion, which is the founder's to decide, so the recommendation must present both branches honestly.
